newsitem.title: USA: Analysts see possible Campbell restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see possible Campbell restructuring.

text.p: Although few surprises are forseen in Campbell Soup Co's fourth quarter earnings, to be reported Thursday, the report also may outline a significant restructuring, analysts said.

In response to a flurry of media reports that it was weighing significant staff cuts and divisional sales, Campbell has acknowledged that it has been conducting a structural review with an aim to "unlock resources." But company spokesman Jerry Buckley said Tuesday that he could not comment on a timetable for announcing the results of the review.
"It's ongoing. That's about all I can say right now," he said.

Campbell already has told employees it expects there will be "less work to do" after the review is complete, spokesman Kevin Lowery said. The review is aimed at eliminating inefficiencies and reinvesting the savings back into the business, he said. Analysts have speculated Campbell's Swanson frozen foods unit could be a target for divestiture.
Merrill Lynch analyst Leonard Teitelbaum said a restructuring could be announced as soon as Thursday's annual earnings report but could also await further evaluation.
"It wouldn't surprise me one way or the other," he said. Company officials have made clear in meetings with analysts that "everything is up for grabs," he said.

Teitelbaum said Campbell Chairman David Johnson has stated his intention to bring Campbell's financial performance into the top ranks of branded consumer goods companies, rather than just the top ranks of food companies. To do that, Teitelbaum said, a hard look at issues such as capital control and return on assets is essential. "After a decade of really thrashing the income statement, I think about all of the food industry is looking at the balance sheet," he said.

Analysts expect Campbell to report earnings of $0.64 a share for the fourth quarter ended July 31, 1996, according to the average of those surveyed by I/B/E/S. That would compare with $0.57 a year earlier. Full-year earnings are forecast at $3.13 a share, against $2.80 the previous year.
Campbell has relentlessly sought to improve efficiency and cut costs under Johnson, who took over as chief executive officer in 1990 and was named chairman in 1993.

That drive was given a new boost this year when Campbell hired as its Chief Financial Officer Basil Anderson, who had been a key engineer of Scott Paper Co's dramatic downsizing and restructuring under then-Chairman Al Dunlap.
Johnson's term expires in July 1997, and it is not known whether he will continue past then -- which analysts said could add impetus to the restructuring effort.
"I'm locked in for the year (to 1997), and I've not made up my mind beyond that. I'm having a great time," Johnson told analysts earlier this year.
One analyst, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Campbell may want to wait until later in the year to announce its restructuring, given Anderson's relatively short tenure.
Doing so would increase chances for a restructuring more substantial than simply job cuts, the analyst said. "If they wait, I think it would be more meaningful."
